title: PEAK
genre: online co-op (1–4 players) climbing / survival comedy ('friendslop'), procedurally varied daily maps, physics/ragdoll
developer: Aggro Crab + Landfall (credited as Team PEAK)
team_size: 7 people built the core: 3 from Aggro Crab + 4 from Landfall during a month-long retreat in Seoul [CONFIRMED – devs via Game Developer/PC Gamer]; more staff from both studios joined for post-launch updates
country: USA (Aggro Crab, Seattle) + Sweden (Landfall, Stockholm); developed in Seoul, South Korea
developer_background: Experienced indie studios. Aggro Crab: Going Under (2020), Another Crab's Treasure (2024; Peak outsold it in under a week). Landfall: Clustertruck, Totally Accurate Battle Simulator, Content Warning (2024 friendslop hit, 6.2M free claims in 24h). Landfall used the same 'travel-and-jam' process for Content Warning. Peak was pitched in a Swedish hot tub ~mid-2024 and treated as a 'side hustle'; both studios agreed to ship whatever they made in Korea.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3527290/PEAK/ (PC only as of research date; Xbox port only rumoured in June 2025)
business_model: premium $7.99, launched with a 38% discount (~$4.95, 'impulse spend'); later sales at $4.95; free content updates (e.g. Mesa update Aug 2025, 'The Final Ascent' update ~2026-08-11); cosmetics/merch
units_or_downloads: 100,000 in 24h; 1,000,000 in 6 days (~2025-06-22) [CONFIRMED – Landfall on X via PC Gamer/Game Developer]; 2,000,000 in 9 days [CONFIRMED – devs via PC Gamer/GamesRadar]; ~4.5M within a month (early July 2025) [CONFIRMED-ish – GameDiscoverCo citing Steam back-end data shared by devs]; 5M+ less than a month after launch [CONFIRMED – Aggro Crab]; ~9.7M copies + $55M revenue (mid-Aug 2025) [ESTIMATE – Alinea Analytics]; 10M+ (2025-08-19) [CONFIRMED – announced by Geoff Keighley on stage at Gamescom Opening Night Live; based on analyst data, not a direct dev post]; '11 million copies sold on Steam' [per GamesRadar headline, 2026, date not pinned]; 20M+ players by the one-year anniversary (June 2026) [CONFIRMED – Aggro Crab interview with Dev Dive via Insider Gaming/Gamereactor; players ≠ paid copies]. Raijin tracker shows only ~7M (2026-06-04) [ESTIMATE – Raijin, likely underestimate]. Lead '15.7M units / $87–92M' could not be sourced.
peak_concurrent_players: 170,759 on 2025-08-17 (after Mesa update + $4.95 sale) [CONFIRMED – SteamDB via press; trackers show 169,910–170,645]; earlier record 114,492 on 2025-07-06. ~40.7k on 2026-08-31 [SteamPulse]. Lead of ~170k verified.
steam_reviews: ~326,000 reviews, 95% positive ('Overwhelmingly Positive') as of 2026-06-04 [Raijin]; 15k reviews at 92% in the first few days (June 2025)
implied_review_multiplier: ~31–34 [ESTIMATE – 10–11M units ÷ ~326k reviews (June 2026); the 10M figure is from Aug 2025, so the true ratio at matching dates is likely somewhat higher]. Surprisingly low for a cheap viral co-op game; players clearly review a lot. Using 20M 'players' instead gives ~61 (players, not buyers).
gross_revenue: ≈ $62M Steam gross [ESTIMATE – 11M units × $5.67 avg realised price, derived from Alinea's $55M ÷ 9.7M; heavy launch/sale discounting means 0.75 × list ($6.00) would overstate it slightly]. Trackers: $55M+ at 9.7M copies (Aug 2025) [ESTIMATE – Alinea]; $56.1M (2026-06-04) [ESTIMATE – Raijin]. Unsourced lead of $87–92M not confirmed.
net_revenue: ≈ $44M [ESTIMATE – $62.4M gross; Steam tiered cut (30% first $10M, 25% $10–50M, 20% above) leaves $46.9M × 0.93 = $43.6M], shared between Aggro Crab and Landfall (split undisclosed).
production_cost: < $200,000 total [CONFIRMED – Game Developer: 'How co-op climbing hit Peak achieved 2 million sales for less than $200,000' (developer figures; see sources)]. Cross-check: 7 people × ~1–4 months × $6k ≈ $42k–170k [ESTIMATE].
development_time: Core built in a ~4-week jam in Seoul starting Feb 2025; ~4 months total to launch 2025-06-16 [CONFIRMED – devs via PC Gamer/Game Developer]. Teaser went live only ~4 days before release; announce-to-launch about one week.
why_popular: Simple, instantly understandable goal (climb the mountain together) with stamina management, ragdoll physics and comedic failure; no monster, the climb is the antagonist; built for voice chat and teamwork (revives, ropes, shared food); extremely watchable for streamers; $8 price (under $5 at launch) made it an impulse buy for whole friend groups; daily changing maps; arrived as 'friendslop' (Lethal Company, Content Warning, R.E.P.O.) was peaking.
marketing_channels: Almost no pre-launch hype (only 29,384 wishlists at launch, teaser ~4 days before release); growth came after launch from Twitch/YouTube streamers and TikTok/short-form clips of ragdoll falls; existing Landfall/Aggro Crab audiences and social accounts; Steam top-seller/algorithm momentum; launch discount; summer sale and later $4.95 discounts plus content updates (Mesa) that set new CCU records. Valve advised against a Content Warning-style free day. Award nominations kept it visible (devs publicly rebutted false AI-use claims). | FOLLOW-UP 2026-10-08: a single TikTok clip by @manticatol (2025-06-19) reached ~3.6M views and ~539k likes in ten days [ESTIMATE – Know Your Meme]; Twitch later added an exclusive PEAK badge.
engine: Unity [CONFIRMED – devs describe baking maps in the Unity Editor (GDC talk via Game Developer)]
art_style: stylised low-poly / soft-shaded 3D with bright colours, cartoony scout characters, physics-driven active ragdolls
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the bulk of gameplay code (stamina/climbing systems, items, procedural level assembly, Steam lobbies, UI), generate low-poly props and environment pieces, SFX and music, and iterate quickly on small features. | AI cannot: nail active-ragdoll climbing feel and physics sync across 4 networked players (the hard part, where Landfall's prior tech was a big advantage), comedic timing, map design that produces emergent co-op moments, netcode debugging under real latency, and the luck/streamer virality. PEAK's team had years of physics-co-op experience and existing audiences. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 (or Godot 4) + Steamworks lobbies with Netcode for GameObjects/Fishnet/Photon Fusion (or Steam P2P via Facepunch.Steamworks), PuppetMaster-style active ragdoll asset or custom joints, Meshy/Tripo for low-poly props, ElevenLabs SFX, Suno music.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 6–10 weeks, $300–$900 (1 biome, 2–4 player online co-op climbing with stamina + ragdoll, Steam lobbies; tool subscriptions, asset packs for ragdoll/netcode $50–$200, Steam Direct $100)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 4–8 months, $3,000–$12,000 (3–4 biomes, items, daily maps, cosmetics; freelance 3D/character polish $1–5k, playtest sessions, streamer outreach/key distribution and trailer; excludes developer's own living costs)

data_conflicts: Units: 10M+ (Aug 2025, Keighley/Alinea) and '11M on Steam' (GamesRadar 2026 headline) vs Raijin's ~7M (June 2026), which is clearly an underestimate; used 10–11M. The lead of 15.7M units / $87–92M could not be found in any source and was not used. '20M players' (June 2026, Aggro Crab) counts players, not purchases. Price: list $7.99 but launched at 38% off (~$4.95) and frequently discounted, so used Alinea's implied ~$5.67 realised price instead of 0.75 × list. Dev time: '4 weeks' (core jam) vs '~4 months' (total) – both reported. Peak CCU: 169,910–171k across trackers; used SteamDB-reported 170,759. CROSS-CHECK 2026-10-08: the '< $200k' cost is supported by the Game Developer headline in the sources (and ~$200k by Italian press); a second independent search did not surface the article again.
notes: Most relevant Group A case for a solo/AI creator: <$200k cost, ~4 months, tiny team, no pre-launch marketing (29k wishlists), cheap price, built for streamers and friend groups. But the team had deep prior co-op/physics tech (Landfall) and existing audiences. Friendslop is now crowded (How To Market A Game, July 2026: top titles take >50% of the player base then fade to ~10% within 3–9 months), so design the hook for clip-ability and keep scope tiny. Aggro Crab has since announced another co-op online game, Crashout Crew.
